# CHEM 1210 Problem Set 3: Composition of Substances and Solutions

**Due Friday September 25, 2026 at 5:00 pm.** Total: 40 points. Show every step with units and report answers to the correct number of significant figures. Use atomic masses H 1.008, C 12.01, O 16.00, Na 22.99, Cl 35.45 g/mol.

## Problem 1 (10 points)

How many grams of sodium chloride (NaCl, molar mass 58.44 g/mol) are needed to prepare 250.0 mL of a 0.350 M NaCl solution?

## Problem 2 (10 points)

A compound contains 40.92% carbon, 4.58% hydrogen and 54.50% oxygen by mass. Determine its empirical formula. Show the mole ratios you used.

## Problem 3 (10 points)

Explain the difference between an empirical formula and a molecular formula. Give one example of a compound whose two formulas differ, and state the relationship between the molar masses.

## Problem 4 (10 points)

When you calculate molarity, why must you use the volume of the final solution rather than the volume of the solvent you started with? Describe in two or three sentences how you would prepare the solution in Problem 1 in a volumetric flask.
